source_classification: Selected definitions have no NONMATCHING markers in these committed translation units. File comments mentioning X70 describe donor provenance, not the target qualification. Function extents below are X-M1 rows and their hashes were independently computed from the owner-supplied plain image.
behavior: RFC 3526 group 5, generator 2, 192-byte big-endian public and shared values.
DHKey is SHA256(shared), KDK is HMAC-SHA256(DHKey,N1||EnrolleeMAC||N2).
KDF concatenates HMAC-SHA256(KDK,BE32(counter)||Wi-Fi Easy and Secure Key Derivation||BE32(640)); AuthKey=32, KeyWrapKey=16, EMSK=32 bytes.
Authenticator and final key-wrap-authenticator are eight-byte HMAC prefixes. Key-wrap-authenticator TLV is 101e0008 and must be last.
Encrypted settings contain IV then AES-128-CBC ciphertext with PKCS padding. Output excludes the verified KWA and padding.
Password halves produce 16-byte HMAC prefixes. Commitments authenticate secret nonce, selected half, enrollee public key, registrar public key.
intentional_owned_changes: Private candidates outside 2..p-2 or equal to subgroup order q=(p-1)/2 require a new random candidate rather than clearing their top byte. Exponent q would publish one and can produce predictable shared p-1 with a non-subgroup peer.
Public values outside 2..p-2 and shared values zero or one are rejected.
PKCS padding length must be 1..16; stock allows zero and can accept longer same-byte tails.
Authentication tags and commitments use subtle constant-time equality; padding checks inspect all sixteen final bytes.

Retained private exponents, shared-value buffers, derived key material, password halves and secret nonces are zeroized; decrypted buffers are cleared on authentication failure. Caller-owned password and successful plaintext buffers remain the caller's lifecycle responsibility. RustCrypto HMAC/SHA256 and bigint exponentiation internal temporaries and compiler-created copies are not claimed to be comprehensively scrubbed.
The caller must verify the enclosing message Authenticator before decrypting settings. Padding failure and KWA failure paths are not constant-time relative to one another.
integration: Canonical wrapper crate replacement/vendor_protocol/wireless_crypto, its Cargo.lock and wireless_crypto.nix pin the dependencies. The raw-rustc/Bazel integration supplies extern xm1_wireless_crypto; this module imports its crypto crate reexports. The enclosing crypto module declares crypto::wps and owns the existing super::Aes128 primitive, new(&[u8;16]), encrypt/decrypt(&mut [u8;16]); no scalar CPU callback.

synthetic_vectors.provenance: Generated independently with Node node:crypto HMAC/SHA256/createCipheriv and createDiffieHellman using the canonical getDiffieHellman(modp5) prime, not by this Rust implementation. No target firmware execution.
synthetic_vectors.negative_keywrap_vectors: wireless_crypto_wps_tests.rs rejects_independently_encrypted_bad_or_misplaced_kwa: valid PKCS padding encryptions with incorrect KWA, incorrect KWA header, and misplaced KWA
